term: practical background of linguistic competence or forms of life
definition: Learned practical capacities and shared regularities of action involved in competent participation in a linguistic practice. Further verbal interpretations alone may fail to supply those capacities. This sense concerns competence rather than truth by consensus, universal agreement, cultural homogeneity, inaccessible outsider criticism or an infallible epistemic basis.
note: Stipulative analyst sense, attribution DEFERRED. Actual instantiation of the existential position remains OPEN. Existing interpretation-regress and data-relative criterion theorems constrain supplied formal profiles, not the reality or unique meaning-determining role of this background. No denial of mental occurrence or automatic private-language impossibility; docs/wittgenstein.md.
